exhibits.title: You get this SMS from a mobile number

head.why: Banks usually send official messages from a short sender name, not from a personal mobile number.

parts.t: your HDFC Bank KYC will expire today
parts.why: Fake deadline. Real KYC updates are done in the bank app or branch, with no countdown that ends today.

parts.t: and your account will be blocked.
parts.why: A threat of blocking is a pressure tactic to make you act before you think.
The website is not hdfcbank.com. It ends in .xyz and uses a hyphenated name, which is a lookalike trick.

exhibits.title: A message from an unsaved number

parts.t: I lost my phone and this is my new number.
parts.why: "New number" messages are the usual first step of an impersonation scam. Check by calling the old number.

parts.t: I am in the hospital and need ₹15,000 urgently.
parts.why: An emergency plus urgent money is built to make you pay before you think.

parts.t: Send it to my friend's UPI ID, he is helping me.
parts.why: Payment goes to a third person you do not know.

parts.t: Don't call, my phone mic is broken.
parts.why: They avoid a call because your voice check would expose them.

head.why: Real Indian government sites end in .gov.in. This is a .com lookalike.

parts.t: Your income tax refund of ₹45,820 is approved.
parts.why: Unexpected money is bait. Check refunds only on the official portal that you log in to yourself.

parts.t: Claim within 12 hours or it will be cancelled.
parts.why: A short deadline is pressure.

parts.t: Enter your card number, expiry and ATM PIN on the form to receive the refund.
parts.why: Nobody needs your card PIN to pay you. A PIN only lets money out.
An .apk is an app file. Real offices never send apps by email or chat.

exhibits.title: A page opened from a link

head.why: The real address would end in paytm.com. This site belongs to "co-secure-refund.top".

parts.why: Surprise prizes are bait to get you to act.
A countdown timer creates panic.

parts.t: Enter your UPI PIN to receive the money.
parts.why: A PIN only sends money. You never need it to receive.
Trust badges are easy to fake. RBI does not "verify" websites like this.

exhibits.title: A buyer on a selling app

parts.t: I am an army officer posted far away so I cannot meet.
parts.why: "Officer posted far away" is a common story to explain why they cannot meet. A genuine buyer can send a relative or pay on delivery.

parts.t: I will pay the full price now.
I am sending a QR code. Scan it and enter your PIN to receive the money.
parts.why: Every UPI QR makes YOU pay. A PIN is never needed to receive.

parts.t: It shows pending, so enter the PIN again.
parts.why: Pressure to retry. Each PIN entry sends more money out.

parts.t: My courier will collect it tomorrow.
Earn ₹5,000 every day by liking videos!
parts.why: Pay that high for so little work is a lure.

parts.t: Pay ₹500 registration to start your first task.
parts.why: Real jobs do not charge you to start. Small early payouts are bait for bigger deposits.
"Guaranteed" returns are a red flag in any money scheme.
False scarcity pushes you to hurry.
